title: Canonical shift, truncation and cohomology functors on fixed pairs
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with a $t$-structure $t$ [def-weil-t-structure], and let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be an exact functor with coherent shift comparison $s_{K,r}:P(K[r])\simeq(PK)[r]$, preserving both halves in every degree. In the fixed-pair category $\mathcal C^P$ [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], write $c^-_{m,K}:P\tau^{\le m}K\simeq\tau^{\le m}PK$ and $c^+_{m,K}:P\tau^{\ge m}K\simeq\tau^{\ge m}PK$ for the canonical comparisons normalized by the truncation counit and unit. Define the shift functor on fixed pairs by $(K,\theta)[r]=(K[r],\theta[r]\circ s_{K,r})$ and $u\mapsto u[r]$. Define the lifted upper and lower truncation functors by $(K,\theta)\mapsto(\tau^{\le m}K,\tau^{\le m}(\theta)\circ c^-_{m,K})$ and $(K,\theta)\mapsto(\tau^{\ge m}K,\tau^{\ge m}(\theta)\circ c^+_{m,K})$, with maps the corresponding truncations of $u$. Define the lifted cohomology functor in degree $i\in\mathbf Z$ as the composite of lifted $\tau^{\le i}$, lifted $\tau^{\ge i}$, and lifted shift $[i]$, with carrier $(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}K)[i]$ and carrier map $(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}u)[i]$. These are functors of fixed pairs only; no triangulated structure on $\mathcal C^P$ is part of the definition.
